alternatives.label: International politics, political economy & regional change
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response integrates international-relations theory, comparative and EU politics, political economy, law, global and imperial history, sociology, cultural analysis, communication and quantitative and qualitative research. It examines how global political and economic change affects regions and local societies without claiming the comparator’s Arabic-language or Africa-specialist sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum balances politics, political economy, history, sociology, law and cultural analysis. The label reflects that broad international-studies composition and does not imply Arabic proficiency or Africa-area expertise.
progression: Law, Society & Justice and Research Methods & Statistics occur in Year 1 before all selected dependent law and economics courses. Introductory economics, politics, history, sociology and communication precede advanced political economy, EU politics, social theory, media-and-race study, econometrics and conflict analysis. Every course is offered in its assigned Fall-2026-start term, and PPD is in Year 1.

alternatives.label: Global cultures, communication & regional histories
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different route centred on how history, literature, media, language and communication shape cultural identity and regional knowledge. It combines imperial and global histories, comparative cultural expression, African art and heritage, psycholinguistics, rhetoric, sociology, decolonial analysis and advanced humanities research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by history, literature, media, communication, heritage and sociocultural research. The label states that emphasis while avoiding a claim to Arabic-language or comprehensive regional-area training.
progression: Introduction to Brain & Behavior occurs in Year 1 before Psycholinguistics. Introductory history, sociology, literature, rhetoric and media study precede advanced social theory, persuasive communication, race and media, museums, historical research, literary interpretation and art-historical research. Every course is offered in its assigned term, and PPD is in Year 1.
alternatives.distinctness: The cultural-history route differs from the closest response by 13 courses / 97.5 EC in each direction. It replaces most economics, politics and governance study with literature, media, language, heritage and advanced humanities research; the difference follows directly from its cultural and regional-history concept.

alternatives.label: International politics, conflict & global justice
alternatives.concept: A third defensible route concentrating on international order and the institutions used to govern conflict and injustice. It combines international relations, public international and EU law, human rights, comparative constitutional systems, political economy, security history, peace and conflict, radicalisation, data analysis and qualitative and historical research.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has a clear concentration in politics, law, conflict, justice and evidence-based governance. The label reflects that concentration without claiming diplomacy training or a regional-language specialisation.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is earlier: GOSGATE102 in semester 1 precedes international, criminal, constitutional and EU law, and BENGATE102 in semester 2 precedes International Macroeconomics and Econometrics. Personal & Professional Development is in semester 2. Introductory political, legal and economic study precedes advanced EU politics, conflict, extremism, machine learning and the research seminar; Introduction to Data Science precedes Machine Learning. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: The conflict-and-justice route differs from the closest response by 10 courses / 75 EC and from the cultural-history route by 19 courses / 142.5 EC in each direction. Its law, security, radicalisation and data-analysis sequence is a substantive third organising choice.

selection.assessment: Three complete and substantively distinct UCR programmes are defensible. The closest response combines international politics, political economy, regional history and cultural analysis. The second reorganises the evidence around culture, communication and regional histories, and the third around conflict, law and global justice; all pairwise differences exceed the 30-EC floor. The formal regional directions were also assessed as a language-based area-expertise candidate. UCR cannot reproduce the comparator’s Arabic sequence or provide balanced specialist coverage across all eight regions, so no programme is labelled as Africa/Arabic or comprehensive area studies. The maximum of three alternatives is reached without manufacturing a fourth.

Both provide world-historical context for contemporary international developments.
History of Empires addresses imperial structures central to African history, but it remains comparative rather than an Africa survey.
Both train source-based historical research and the analysis of historical evidence.
African Art & Heritage provides substantive study of African visual cultures, colonial collecting, diaspora and cultural memory, while not teaching Arabic.
Both develop communication across differing cultural and social contexts; UCR does so through multilingual community-based rhetoric and storytelling.
Both examine how media technologies shape the circulation and interpretation of humanities knowledge.
Both critically analyse culture, representation, identity and power; UCR concentrates on race across film, photography and music.
Both study language as a structured human practice; UCR concentrates on cognitive processes and bilingualism rather than sociolinguistic variation.
The selected thematic seminar integrates art, literature and law around rights; no single UCR course combines that exact content.

notes.text: Leiden International Studies combines politics, economics, history and culture with a selected regional area and a cumulative language sequence. UCR offers substantial international politics, political economy, history, culture, law, conflict and research study, but the current curriculum has no Arabic course and does not reproduce the Africa-specific language-and-area sequence. The UCR programmes therefore retain an explicit regional-language gap.

The Leiden pathway organises interdisciplinary study around the Africa area, Arabic language progression, 30 EC of open choice and an area-specific thesis. UCR distributes related content across individually selected politics, economics, law, history, sociology, communication, literature, media and heritage courses. Its programmes are feasible compositions rather than formal regional tracks, and optional independent research is shown only as the standardized comparison element.
